title: Ringed-site resolving tensor presentation and canonical signed derived symmetry
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small relative to the universe of its module sheaves and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use the category $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal M)$ with localization $Q$ in the chosen morphism universe [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ')$ for the direct-sum total tensor with differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_{Q'}$ on bidegree $(p,q)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $\mathcal P_R$ be the full subcategory of K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex] all of whose terms are flat module sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. A resolving tensor presentation $T$ consists of a bifunctor $T:D(\mathcal M)\times D(\mathcal M)\to D(\mathcal M)$ and a natural representative isomorphism $\rho_{P,Q'}:Q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ')\xrightarrow{\sim}T(QP,QQ')$ on $\mathcal P_R\times\mathcal P_R$. This is presentation data for the specified K-flat localization, with no boundedness or completion requirement and no equality imposed on the site object and morphism universes.

A signed total swap $\chi_{P,Q'}:\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ')\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}(Q'\otimes_RP)$ means one whose restriction to each bidegree summand is the ordinary sheaf tensor swap multiplied by $(-1)^{pq}$. A derived symmetry $\sigma:T\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{swap}\circ T$ is canonical if on every pair of resolving complexes it satisfies $\sigma_{QP,QQ'}\circ\rho_{P,Q'}=\rho_{Q',P}\circ Q(\chi_{P,Q'})$ for a signed total swap. Define $\mathrm{derivedTensorSymmetry}(R,T)$ to be this uniquely determined canonical derived symmetry, supplied by descent of the signed total swap. The existing uniqueness construction is used; no freely chosen symmetry or additional tensor functor is introduced.
